messages.content: how to get the information of an interface?

function.name: telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get
function.description: Retrieves specified telemetry information for a network interface within a given fabric, node, and pod, filtered by the interface and information types. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit the nodes pertaining to the given fabric name.

nodeId.description: The identifier of the node to limit the results pertaining to the given node ID.

podId.description: The identifier of the pod to limit the results pertaining to the given pod ID.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit the results pertaining to the given interface type.

infoType.description: The type of information to retrieve about the interface.

message.content:
To pull telemetry data for a specific interface you’ll use the **`telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get`** function.  
It needs five pieces of information:

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `fabricName` | Name of the fabric (e.g., `"core-fabric"`). |
| `nodeId` | Numeric ID of the node (e.g., `101`). |
| `podId` | Numeric ID of the pod (e.g., `5`). |
| `interfaceType` | Type of interface you’re querying – one of: `"svi"`, `"ethernet"`, `"loopback"`, or `"port‑channel"`. |
| `infoType` | What kind of data you want – one of: `"interfaces"`, `"status"`, `"statistics"`, or `"errors"`. |

### Example Call

```python
result = telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get({
    "fabricName": "core-fabric",
    "nodeId": 101,
    "podId": 5,
    "interfaceType": "ethernet",
    "infoType": "status"
})
print(result)
```

This would return the current status of all Ethernet interfaces on node 101 in pod 5 of the “core‑fabric”.

### Common Usage Patterns

| Goal | `infoType` |
|------|------------|
| List all interfaces on a node | `"interfaces"` |
| Get operational state (up/down) | `"status"` |
| Retrieve counters like packets/bytes | `"statistics"` |
| Check error counts | `"errors"` |

Just replace the placeholder values (`fabricName`, `nodeId`, etc.) with your environment’s specifics, and the function will fetch the requested telemetry data.
